answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via graph-theoretic credit networks. Identities form signed interaction links across a mutual trust bridge, advancing past a validation terrace to gain routing capacity. Confining flow within a hardened walnut boundary restricts throughput across network cuts, forcing attackers to acquire scarce reciprocal trust from honest peers per identity. However, this mechanism disadvantages legitimate newcomers and entrenches early incumbents.
